BACKGROUND The Forest Service seeks to establish a pilot considering third-party administrator(s) to verify personnel qualifications, excluding all aviation assets. This RFI supports planning and does not establish a particular implementation model. The Forest Service administers national and regional contracting programs that provide contracted resources in support of wildland fire suppression and other emergency incident operations. Contracted resources may be required to demonstrate that personnel assigned to incidents possess qualifications, training, experience, certifications, licenses, medical credentials, or other documentation established by applicable agreements, solicitations, policy, or Government-approved qualification standards. Qualification documentation may currently be reviewed through multiple Government offices, programs, or other approved processes. The Forest Service is exploring whether independent verification of contractor personnel qualifications could improve consistency, timeliness, authenticity of supporting records, and auditability while reducing duplicate submissions and Government workload. The Government is specifically interested in understanding whether industry has the capability to perform this function at national scale while preserving appropriate Government oversight and decision-making authority. This effort may result in a one-year pilot program for the Government. 2. PURPOSE OF THIS MARKET RESEARCH The Forest Service seeks information on independent review against Government-established requirements, documented verification results, and referrals for Government action. The contemplated service would verify contractor personnel qualification documentation against Government-established requirements, including the authenticity and applicability of supporting training records. The service would not include delivering training, approving training providers or instructors, auditing course delivery as a separate service, or inspecting equipment. The Government has not determined that this function will be outsourced. Responses may inform the feasibility of this service, division of responsibilities, acquisition strategy, commercial practices, pricing, small business participation, information protection, quality assurance, and transition planning. The Government has not selected a records system or determined whether a future procurement is appropriate. 3. CONCEPTUAL REQUIREMENT For purposes of this RFI, assume a nationwide service to verify wildfire contractor personnel qualification documentation against Government-established requirements. Supporting documentation may include training and experience records, position task books, certifications, licenses, and other evidence required for the applicable position. The service would not include providing training, separately approving training providers or instructors, or assessing contractor or equipment readiness. Respondents should identify their capabilities, coverage, and limitations. The service would use Government-designated, approved methods for receiving records and reporting verification results. This RFI does not request development, acquisition, hosting, or operation of a new information system or commercial platform. Identify technology dependencies separately. Potential services could include the following: A. Qualification Documentation Review Review documentation submitted by contractors against qualification requirements established by the Government. Documentation could include training and experience records, position qualification records, task books, certifications, licenses, equipment operator qualifications, and other evidence required by the applicable contract or agreement. Where required, review would be limited to necessary evidence of medical clearance, fitness, identity, or personnel affiliation using Government-approved procedures. Respondents should identify ways to confirm required status without collecting underlying medical records, unnecessary identity documents, or other sensitive information. B.
